attempts.raw_response: The inquest heard further that Dr Pantke identified multiple systemic failures in the care provided to Ms Bowles, including a lack of clear communication between departments and insufficient follow-up protocols for patients discharged with high-risk conditions. The coroner noted that had appropriate monitoring been maintained, Ms Bowles may have survived. The report emphasised the need for improved handover procedures and clearer guidelines for post-discharge supervision of vulnerable patients. Dr Pantke concluded that the failures represented a significant departure from accepted medical practice, and recommended immediate implementation of enhanced monitoring systems and regular audits of discharge planning processes to prevent future tragedies. The trust acknowledged the findings and pledged to implement the recommended changes.

pair.human_continuation: "The contributing factor to all of these issues was a lack of clear national guidance on who provides physical health monitoring and care coordination to people with severe risk eating disorders," she added. The inquest has heard the recorded cause of Ms Bowles' death was pneumonia and a pathology report said her eating disorder was likely to have contributed. The court heard Ms Bowles had also been diagnosed with obsessive compulsive disorder, depression and agoraphobia. The inquest continues. If you are affected by any of the issues in this story, you can talk in confidence to eating disorders charity Beat by calling its adult helpline on 0808 801 0677 or youth helpline on 0808 801 0711.
pair.prefix: Her report stated the monitoring following her discharge from the AEDS was "inadequate and on the balance of probabilities these inadequacies contributed to her death". Dr Pantke's report also found on the balance of probabilities she believed "shortcomings" in an assessment on 24 August 2017 "and the absence of urgency to act on the results and implement safeguards contributed to Ms Bowles's death".
